title: Prompt Component Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Classification activity in which learners label each of the ten sentences of one working research prompt as a clear instruction, constraint, output format, role, or few-shot example. Each label gets one attempt with immediate feedback and a reason; the run ends with a score out of 10, a mastery statement at 8 of 10, and a tally of how many sentences carry each component.

educational.topic: The components of a prompt: clear instructions, constraints, output format, role, and few-shot examples
learningObjectives: Distinguish which prompt component, clear instruction, constraint, output format, role, or few-shot example, each of ten prompt sentences carries, with at least 8 of 10 classified correctly
Recognize that constraints are the most numerous component in a well-specified research prompt
prerequisites: Clear instructions, constraints, and output format

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML selects and buttons reachable with the Tab key; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check or X symbols as well as a blue/orange color-blind-safe palette; all body text is 16 px.

controls.label: Component
controls.purpose: Chooses Clear instruction, Constraint, Output format, Role, or Few-shot example for the highlighted sentence. Disabled after Submit.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Commits the single attempt for the highlighted sentence. Enabled when a component is chosen.

controls.label: Next Sentence / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after Submit. Highlights the next sentence, and after sentence 10 shows the score and the component tally.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Decomposition of one working prompt into its parts with one attempt per sentence and immediate explanatory feedback
keyQuestions: Which component of the prompt does this sentence carry?
Does this sentence limit the answer or describe its shape?
Does a role sentence add knowledge or only a viewpoint?
commonMisconceptions: A sentence that sets a length is part of the output format, when it is a constraint.
A role sentence also adds domain knowledge.
An example is only decoration and does not specify behavior.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score of at least 8 of 10 labels matching the answer key is evidence of mastery
Learner explains why sentence 3 is a constraint and sentence 6 an output format
